output.name: Ulkun

anatomy.part: right corner of the rim, where the handle springs and the spill begins
low left of the pot's belly
foot of the handle, the brightest star of the figure
the tip of the spilled salt falling past the belly

output.myth: Every trader keeps a salt pot in the hold, and into it goes the crew's share: one pinch from every catch and every sale. Ulkun is the pot the sky keeps. Hesk the Reel counts the pinches on her string, and she counts them twice, because she is patient and the sea is not. Once a moon the pot is tipped. That is when Sil has gone dark, searching the water for her brother Aun. Tavo the Gale comes down the road and leans on the rim. The salt runs out over the dark, and the crew says it is the share spilling for those who went aloft and never sat down to eat. Do not laugh when Tavo does this. He does not like it, and he will tip the next pot too. Before you sleep, set one pinch aside for whoever is out past the Leeward light, and count it twice. Hesk is still counting.
output.verse:
Ulkun spills the share
where the new moon leaves the pot
Hesk counts each grain twice.
